prompt: In a histogram, a region where bins are very tall is called a:
hint: Tall bins mean that many data values fall close together in that part of the number line.

hints.text: Tall bins mean that many data values fall close together in that part of the number line.
The word you want describes a bunch of things grouped tightly together, such as a group of stars or grapes.
A region of tall bins is called a cluster.

explanation: The height of a histogram bin tells how many values fall in that interval.
Several very tall bins side by side mean that a lot of the data is bunched in that region.
A place where data values bunch together is called a cluster.
